Rabies is present in Florida bats.
Florida DOH confirmed 30 rabid bats in 2024 and 42 in 2025 among animals that may have exposed people or pets, plus a few more found through surveillance testing (
DOH 2024
DOH 2025
). If anyone may have touched a bat, call your county health department before releasing it.
Guano:
FWC says histoplasmosis from bat guano in a building has never been reported in Florida, but the CDC advises wearing a respirator around guano in tight spaces. See our
bat guano cleanup guide
Skip ultrasonic devices.
UF/IFAS says they don't repel bats.
Next steps:
bat removal
bats in the attic
and
bat removal in Tampa

faq.question: What kind of bats live under barrel tile roofs in Florida?

children.text: Usually Brazilian free-tailed bats. UF/IFAS says they're found throughout Florida and roost under barrel roof tiles, in attics and under bridges.

faq.question: Can I seal my tile roof to keep bats out?

children.text: Not while bats are inside, and not during maternity season. Bats have to be excluded first with one-way devices, from August 15 to April 15, then the openings are sealed.

faq.question: Do bats damage tile roofs?

children.text: Bats don't chew like rodents, but their droppings and staining build up below the roost, and a colony that's sealed in can die inside the roof.

faq.question: Is it legal to remove bats from my roof in summer?

children.text: Not without a special FWC permit. FWC says excluding bats during maternity season, April 16 through August 14, is otherwise illegal.

title: Rats in the Walls: How to Tell and What to Do in Florida
author: Josh Holmberg
excerpt: Scratching inside the walls at night usually means rats using the wall as a highway between the attic and food. Here's how to confirm it, how they get in, and why bait often ends with a smell.

children.text: The short answer:

scratching or scurrying inside a wall at night, with droppings or gnawing nearby, usually means rats. In Florida it's often roof rats moving between the attic and food below. Seal the gaps they use, then trap the rats inside along their paths. Poison can leave a dead rat in the wall. Call (844) 264-6254.
How to tell it's rats
Night noise.
UF/IFAS says rats are most active at night, and Florida DOH says roof rats peak about an hour after sunset and an hour before dawn (
Florida DOH
Droppings or urine stains,
which UF/IFAS calls the usual first signs. Check baseboards, cabinets and under sinks (
UF/IFAS
Rub marks and gnawing.
UF/IFAS Extension in Duval lists droppings, urine, rub marks and gnawing as the tell-tale signs, and DOH describes dark grease stains where rats run.
Sounds that move up and down,
which suggests rats traveling between the attic and floor level.
If you're not sure it's rats, our guide to
what animal is in your attic
compares the usual suspects.
Roof rats or Norway rats?

Florida DOH says roof rats prefer high places such as attics, while Norway rats tend to stay on lower floors. Roof rats are strong climbers: UF/IFAS says they can jump three feet straight up and more than four feet across, and recommends pruning limbs away from the house (
UF/IFAS
). More on telling them apart in
Norway rat vs roof rat
How they get into the walls

UF/IFAS says rats can get through gaps of about half an inch, and DOH notes roof rats need only a hole the size of a quarter. Common routes are roof returns, gaps where pipes and A/C lines go through the wall, and openings under the eaves. UF/IFAS Extension in Duval warns that rodents easily chew through spray foam (
UF/IFAS
). UF/IFAS Extension in Santa Rosa says to close gaps with mortar, concrete, sheet metal or 19-gauge hardware cloth with no openings over ¼ inch (
UF/IFAS
Trap, don't poison, inside walls
Snap traps
are a low-cost option, UF/IFAS Extension in Pinellas says, and glue boards aren't humane because they prolong death (
UF/IFAS
Place traps along walls,
near holes, or across beams and rafters where rats travel, as UF/IFAS advises.
Poison is a last resort.
Pinellas Extension says rodenticides can take several days to kill, and UF/IFAS says toxic baits are legal only for non-native rats and house mice and must be in bait boxes (
UF/IFAS
Why bait can end with a smell
Poisoned rats don't die on the spot. Our
dead animal smell
guide has UF/IFAS's timeline for anticoagulant bait (
UF/IFAS
), and by then a rat may be back inside the wall it lives in. That guide also covers what to do if it happens.
The usual order
Inspect
the roofline, attic and outside walls for every gap.
Seal
the openings, leaving none the rats can still use.
Trap
the rats left inside along their paths, and check the traps often.
Clean up
droppings with gloves and disinfectant, never by sweeping or vacuuming.
See
rat removal
rats in the attic
and
rat removal in Tampa

faq.question: How do I know if rats are in my walls?

children.text: Listen for scratching or scurrying at night, and look for droppings, urine stains, gnaw marks and dark rub marks near baseboards, under sinks and where pipes come through.

faq.question: Will rats in the walls leave on their own?

children.text: Not usually, as long as they have food nearby and a way in. The openings have to be sealed and the rats inside trapped.

faq.question: Should I put poison in the walls?

children.text: UF/IFAS Extension treats poison as a last resort. Poisoned rats can take days to die, often back inside the wall, which leaves a dead rat you can't reach and a smell.

faq.question: Can I fill the holes with spray foam?

children.text: UF/IFAS Extension warns rodents easily chew through spray foam. Use mortar, sheet metal or heavy hardware cloth instead, then trap any rats left inside.

title: How to Clean Up Rat Droppings and Nesting in a Florida Attic
author: Josh Holmberg
excerpt: Rat droppings and nests can carry disease, and health officials say not to sweep or vacuum them. Here are the CDC's steps, what to do with soiled insulation, and when to bring in help.

children.text: The short answer:

air the space out, put on gloves, and soak droppings, urine and nesting material with disinfectant or a bleach mix before you touch them. Wipe them up with paper towels, bag the waste, then mop. Never sweep or vacuum. For a heavy infestation, full protective gear is needed. Call (844) 264-6254 for help.
Why you can't just sweep it up
The CDC says rodent diseases mainly reach people through the air they breathe, and that sweeping or vacuuming droppings, urine or nests can put tiny droplets carrying viruses into the air (
CDC
). Florida DOH gives the same warning about hantavirus: keep the area well ventilated and avoid anything that raises dust, including sweeping and vacuuming (
Florida DOH
Before you start
Find out what you're dealing with.
The CDC says rodent droppings are pointed at one end and often contain hair (
CDC
). Our guide to
what rat poop looks like
helps tell rats from other animals.
Make sure the rats are gone,
or you'll be cleaning again next month. Seal the entry points and trap any rats still inside first (
CDC
Air it out.
For homes and sheds, the CDC says to open doors and windows for half an hour and stay out while it airs (
CDC
Gear up:
rubber or plastic gloves at a minimum. Wash any clothing that may be soiled in hot water with detergent afterward.
Step by step
Mix fresh bleach solution:
1½ cups of household bleach in a gallon of water, which the CDC gives as 1 part bleach to 9 parts water. A household cleaner labeled "disinfectant" also works (
CDC
Spray until everything is very wet
and leave it for 5 minutes, or as long as the label says.
Pick it up with paper towels,
not a broom, and drop them in a covered trash can that gets emptied often.
Nests:
soak the nesting material the same way, then seal it in a plastic bag inside a second bag.
Mop or sponge the area
with disinfectant once the droppings are gone.
Wash your gloved hands
with soap and water or disinfectant before taking the gloves off, then wash your bare hands with warm water and soap.
Insulation, ducts and fabrics

The CDC's advice on insulation is short: if exposed insulation is soiled with urine and droppings, bag it for removal. If rats have been in your heating and cooling system, it says to bring in a professional rodent service. Soiled bedding and clothes go in hot water with detergent, and rugs and upholstery can be shampooed with a commercial disinfectant or steam cleaner (
CDC
How much insulation has to come out depends on how far the nesting and droppings have spread.
When it's too big to do yourself

The CDC calls for extra precautions in homes with a heavy rodent infestation: coveralls, rubber boots or shoe covers, gloves, goggles, and a respirator. It names a half-mask air-purifying respirator with a HEPA filter, or a powered one with HEPA filters (
CDC
). A packed attic in Florida heat, in that gear, is hard work. That's usually the point to call for help.
The health risks in Florida
Hantavirus:
the CDC says the virus can get into the air when fresh urine, droppings or nesting material from an infected rodent is stirred up (
CDC
). Florida DOH says it has been found in cotton rats in Florida, though most human cases have been in the western U.S. (
Florida DOH
Leptospirosis:
Florida DOH says people catch it through water, soil or plants contaminated with the urine of infected animals, or by touching an infected animal's body fluids (
Florida DOH
Food:
the CDC says disease can also spread through food contaminated with rodent waste (
CDC
If you get sick with fever and aches in the weeks after a cleanup, tell your doctor about the rodent exposure (
Florida DOH
). See also
rats in the attic
and
rat removal
, and if the smell is a dead rat, our
dead animal smell guide

faq.question: Can I vacuum rat droppings?

children.text: No. The CDC and Florida DOH both say not to sweep or vacuum droppings, urine or nests, because it puts virus particles into the air. Soak them with disinfectant and wipe them up instead.

faq.question: Is dried rat poop safe to touch?

children.text: Don't assume so. Neither the CDC nor Florida DOH makes an exception for old droppings, so treat them the same way: gloves, a thorough soak with disinfectant, paper towels and a sealed bag.

faq.question: Do I have to replace insulation with rat droppings in it?

children.text: The CDC says soiled exposed insulation should be bagged for removal. How much of an attic needs it depends on how far the nesting and droppings have spread.

faq.question: Why does my attic smell after rats?

children.text: Urine and droppings build up where rats nest and travel, and a rat that died in the attic adds its own smell. Cleaning up the waste and finding any carcass are the first steps.

title: Does Homeowners Insurance Cover Rat or Bat Damage in Florida?
author: Josh Holmberg
excerpt: Standard homeowners policies usually exclude damage from rodents and other pests, but policies differ. Here's what the consumer guides say, what to check in your own policy, and Florida's claim deadlines.

children.text: The short answer:

usually not. The national insurance regulators' group says damage from rats and other infestations isn't typically covered, and a widely used sample policy form (ISO's HO-3) lists vermin and rodents as an exclusion. But policies differ, so read yours and ask your insurer before you assume anything. Call (844) 264-6254 to have the animals removed.
What the consumer guides say
NAIC,
the national association of state insurance regulators: damage caused by termites, rats or other infestations is "not typically covered" (
NAIC
The Insurance Information Institute:
a homeowners policy won't cover damage from lack of maintenance or infestation by termites or other pests, but policies vary, so check yours (
III
A sample standard policy form:
the 1999 ISO HO-3 form the III publishes lists "birds, vermin, rodents, or insects" among the causes of loss to the house and other structures it doesn't insure (
sample HO-3
). Your own policy may be worded differently.
Why it's usually excluded
NAIC's consumer guide puts it this way: a homeowners policy isn't a maintenance contract; it insures against perils such as fire, wind and hail (
NAIC
). Florida's Department of Financial Services puts it plainly: policies don't cover everything, and you need to read the exclusions in your own contract (
Florida DFS
Check your own policy for
The exclusions section,
for words like vermin, rodents, pests, insects, animals or birds.
Ensuing loss or resulting damage language,
which some policies use for damage that follows an excluded cause. How it applies, if at all, is a question for your insurer.
Endorsements
you may have added, and whether your policy is an open-peril (HO-3) or named-peril form.
Your insurer's answer in writing.
If you have questions about how your claim is handled, DFS's toll-free Insurance Consumer Helpline is 1-877-693-5236 (
Florida DFS
If you do file a claim in Florida
Report it on time.
Florida law bars a new or reopened property claim unless notice is given under the policy terms within 1 year after the date of loss, and a supplemental claim within 18 months (
Protect the house.
DFS says you must make reasonable emergency repairs to prevent further damage, take photos of any damaged property, and save all receipts for emergency repairs (
Florida DFS
). Your policy lists your other duties after a loss.
Know the timeline.

Florida's Homeowner Claims Bill of Rights gives you the right to an acknowledgment within 7 days and, within 60 days, full payment, payment of the undisputed portion, or a denial. It also gives free DFS mediation of a disputed claim under most circumstances, subject to certain restrictions (
Fla. Stat. 627.7142
What to do either way
Whatever your policy says, the animals have to go and the openings have to be closed, and that part is on the homeowner (
NAIC
). Photograph the damage, the droppings and the entry points before any work starts, and keep the removal paperwork. For the work itself, see
rat removal
and
bat removal
. For bats, check
Florida's bat laws
first: exclusion without an FWC permit is only allowed from August 15 to April 15.

faq.question: Does homeowners insurance pay for bat removal?

children.text: No official consumer guide says it does. NAIC says damage from rats and other infestations isn't typically covered, and a sample standard policy excludes vermin. Policies differ, so ask your insurer in writing before the work starts.

faq.question: Will insurance cover wiring that rats chewed?

children.text: Don't count on it. A sample standard policy form excludes damage caused by rodents. Whether anything that follows from it is covered depends on your policy's wording, so ask your insurer.

faq.question: How long do I have to file a claim in Florida?

children.text: Florida law bars a property insurance claim unless the insurer gets notice within 1 year after the date of loss. Supplemental claims have 18 months. Report it as soon as you find the damage.

faq.question: Who can I ask about my policy?

children.text: Your agent or insurer first. Florida's Department of Financial Services runs a toll-free Insurance Consumer Helpline at 1-877-693-5236, and offers free mediation for many disputed claims, subject to certain restrictions.

title: Do Bats Hibernate in Florida? What Bats Do in Winter
author: Josh Holmberg
excerpt: Florida's bats don't disappear for the winter. Here's what UF/IFAS and FWC say about bats in the cooler months, why fall and winter are exclusion season, and why a cold snap can pause the work.

children.text: The short answer:

not the way bats up north do. UF/IFAS says bats are active year-round in Florida. That's why fall and winter are the season to get them out of a house, as long as the nights are warm enough: FWC requires overnight lows of 50°F or warmer during an exclusion. Call (844) 264-6254.
Florida bats in winter
UF/IFAS counts 13 bat species in Florida and says they're active year-round (
UF/IFAS
). In Tampa, the city says the Brazilian free-tailed bat, a common bat in the area, stays active all year (
City of Tampa
). So a colony in your attic in July may well still be there in January.
Why winter is exclusion season
Florida law protects bats while they raise their young. FWC bans exclusion from April 16 to August 14, and allows it from August 15 to April 15 (
FWC

). UF/IFAS recommends fall and winter for a bat exclusion in Florida. During the spring and summer pup season, young bats that can't fly yet would be trapped inside and die, and the decay can draw pests such as cockroaches (
UF/IFAS
What a cold snap does to the work
FWC's temperature rule:
one-way exclusion devices stay up for at least four nights in a row with overnight lows forecast at 50°F or above (
FWC
Bats stay in when it's cold.

FWC says bats tend not to leave their roost on windy, cold or rainy nights, and recommends leaving the exclusion devices up for extra nights when that happens. FWC also notes bats can cut back their activity in cool weather and stay in the roost for several days (
FWC
Plan around the forecast.
In a Florida winter, that usually means waiting out a cold front and starting the count again on the warm nights after it.
What not to do in winter
Don't seal holes while bats are inside,
even if you haven't seen them in a while. They're likely still roosting, and sealed-in bats die in the walls or attic.
Don't use ultrasonic devices or repellents.
UF/IFAS says ultrasonic devices don't repel bats.
Don't wait until spring.
Exclusion closes on April 15 and doesn't open again until August 15.
More on the rules in
Florida bat laws
and
bat maternity season
, and on tile roofs in
bats under barrel tile roofs
. See also
bat removal
and
bats in the attic

faq.question: Do bats go away in the winter in Florida?

children.text: Usually not. UF/IFAS says Florida's bats are active year-round, so a colony in the attic generally stays through the cooler months.

faq.question: Can bats be removed from a house in winter?

children.text: Yes. FWC allows exclusion from August 15 to April 15, and UF/IFAS recommends fall and winter. Devices have to stay up four nights with lows of 50°F or warmer.

faq.question: Why does cold weather delay bat exclusion?

children.text: Bats tend not to leave their roost on windy, cold or rainy nights, FWC says, so it recommends leaving the devices up for extra nights when the weather turns.

faq.question: Is it too late to deal with bats after spring arrives?

children.text: FWC bans exclusion from April 16 to August 14, the maternity season, so after April 15 it can't start again until August 15. That's why winter is the time to act.

title: Found a Baby Raccoon in Florida? What to Do, and Why You Can't Keep It
author: Josh Holmberg
excerpt: A baby raccoon on its own usually isn't an orphan. Here's what FWC says to do, when to call a wildlife rehabilitator, why Florida law won't let you raise it, and what to do if the family is in your attic.

children.text: The short answer:

leave it alone and watch from a distance. FWC says baby animals are rarely orphaned; the mother is often nearby. If it's hurt or clearly abandoned, call a wildlife rehabilitator. You can't keep it: Florida never allows injured, orphaned or abandoned native animals as pets. Family in your attic? Call (844) 264-6254.
Is it really an orphan?

FWC says that, generally, a baby animal found on its own should be left alone. Animals are rarely actually orphaned: the parent may be searching for food or watching from a distance. It asks people not to pick up baby animals or take them out of their surroundings (
FWC
Timing helps. UF/IFAS says Florida raccoon litters are generally born in March and April, with three or four young on average (
UF/IFAS
). A young raccoon seen in spring or early summer often has a mother close by.
When to call for help
It's injured,
visibly sick, or in immediate danger, such as in a road or with a pet.
You know the mother is dead,
or you're not sure. A wildlife rehabilitator can tell you whether to step in.
Who to call:
FWC says to note where the animal is and contact a wildlife rehabilitator in your area, or the FWC regional office if you can't reach one. FWC keeps a list of permitted rehabilitators by county (
FWC
Why you can't keep it

Florida law doesn't allow it. FWC says injured, orphaned or abandoned native animals are never eligible to be kept as personal pets in Florida, and pet permits are only issued for animals from a legal source (
FWC
). FWC also says keeping injured or orphaned wildlife longer than it takes to get it to a rehabilitator is a violation of Florida law, and caring for wildlife needs an FWC rehabilitation permit (
FWC
Don't touch it bare-handed
Florida DOH names raccoons and bats as the main wildlife sources of rabies in Florida, usually spread through bites (
Florida DOH
). Even a small raccoon can bite or scratch. If anyone is bitten or scratched, wash the wound with soap and water and call your doctor and county health department.
If the family is in your attic or under your house
A mother raccoon may raise her kits in an attic or under a house. The young have to come out with the mother, not be left behind or sealed in, and the opening is closed after. Our guides to
raccoons in the attic
raccoon mating season in Florida
and
raccoon trapping rules
explain how that works. See also
raccoon removal

faq.question: What do I do if I find a baby raccoon alone?

children.text: Leave it where it is and watch from a distance. FWC says baby animals are rarely orphaned and the mother is often nearby. Call a wildlife rehabilitator only if it's hurt or clearly abandoned.

faq.question: Can I keep a baby raccoon as a pet in Florida?

children.text: No. FWC says injured, orphaned or abandoned native animals are never eligible to be kept as personal pets in Florida.

faq.question: Who takes orphaned raccoons in Florida?

children.text: Wildlife rehabilitators with an FWC permit. FWC lists them by county on its injured and orphaned wildlife page, and its regional offices can help if you can't reach one.

faq.question: When are baby raccoons born in Florida?

children.text: UF/IFAS says Florida raccoon litters are generally born in March and April, with three or four young on average.

title: Can You Kill or Trap a Squirrel in Florida? What the Rules Allow
author: Josh Holmberg
excerpt: A gray squirrel chewing into your attic counts as nuisance wildlife under Florida's rules, which allow trapping with conditions. Fox squirrels are a different story. Here's what FWC allows, and what it doesn't.

children.text: The short answer:

for a gray squirrel causing damage, yes, within limits. FWC lets property owners live-trap nuisance wildlife if they check traps every 24 hours, and the squirrel can only be released on their own property or permitted land. Fox squirrels can't be trapped or taken without FWC authorization. Call (844) 264-6254.
When a squirrel counts as nuisance wildlife
Florida's rule (68A-9.010) defines nuisance wildlife as an animal that causes or is about to cause property damage, threatens public safety, or causes an annoyance in, under or on a building (
FWC
). A gray squirrel nesting in your attic or chewing a soffit fits. FWC says gray squirrels are active by day and Florida also has fox squirrels and southern flying squirrels (
FWC
What the rule allows
No permit for most cases.
FWC says property owners, and trappers they hire, don't need to notify FWC or get its approval to take most nuisance wildlife from private property (
FWC
Live traps,
inspected at least once every 24 hours. Any other animal caught has to be let go on the spot.
A decision within 24 hours.
A live-caught animal has to be released legally or humanely euthanized within 24 hours of capture or trap inspection.
Firearms only where allowed,
in daylight. FWC notes that firing a gun may be prohibited in some cities and residential areas, so check with local law enforcement first.
Where a trapped squirrel can go

Gray squirrels are native, so they can be released, but only two ways, FWC says: on the property where they were caught (one contiguous piece of land), or on land of at least 40 contiguous acres in the same county, with the landowner's written permission in hand (
FWC
). Dropping one at a park or along a road without the landowner's written permission isn't legal. Our
Florida wildlife trapping rules
guide covers the details.
New FWC trapping rules start December 31, 2026.
They change trap check times, allow remote (camera) checks, and require most people who trap to complete FWC's annual registration and training, which FWC says is
at no cost

. A homeowner using one regular-size cage trap (door up to 20 by 28 inches) on their own property, to catch nuisance or non-native wildlife, doesn't need registration, training or reporting. Nuisance animals moved off site must be released or put down within 12 hours of the trap check, down from 24. Details at
MyFWC.com/TrappingRules
Fox squirrels are different
FWC says fox squirrels may not be taken or pursued, and its rule (68A-29.002) covers their young and nests too, so the nuisance-wildlife rule above doesn't apply to them without FWC authorization (
FWC

). The Big Cypress fox squirrel in southwest Florida is state-designated Threatened. The southern fox squirrel, once called Sherman's fox squirrel and found in Central Florida, came off the Species of Special Concern list in 2018 but is still under FWC's conservation guidelines (
FWC
). If the squirrel in your attic is a big, black-faced fox squirrel, get advice before doing anything.
What about hunting season?
Gray squirrels are also a game species, with FWC hunting rules and bag limits (
FWC
). Those rules are about hunting, which generally needs a license and isn't the same thing as dealing with a squirrel in your house.
The part that actually fixes it
Removing a squirrel without closing the hole it chewed just leaves room for the next one. Check for a nest of young before anything is sealed, and close the roofline afterward. See
squirrels in the attic
squirrel removal
and
why squirrels come back

faq.question: Is it legal to trap a squirrel in Florida?

children.text: Yes, if it's nuisance wildlife on your property. FWC allows live traps without a permit for most cases, checked at least every 24 hours, with release only where the rule allows.

faq.question: Can I relocate a squirrel to a park?

children.text: Not without written permission. FWC allows release only on the property where it was caught, or on 40 or more contiguous acres in the same county with the landowner's written permission in hand.

faq.question: Are fox squirrels protected in Florida?

children.text: Yes. FWC says fox squirrels may not be taken or pursued in Florida without its authorization. The southern fox squirrel, once called Sherman's fox squirrel, was removed from the Species of Special Concern list in 2018 but stays under FWC's conservation guidelines, and the Big Cypress fox squirrel is state-designated Threatened.

faq.question: Do the trapping rules change in 2026?

children.text: Yes. FWC's new trapping rules start December 31, 2026, with registration and training for most trappers and a 12-hour limit for animals taken off site. Homeowners using one regular-size cage trap on their own land are exempt from registration, training and reporting when trapping nuisance or non-native wildlife.

title: Do Rats Come Out During the Day? What a Daytime Rat Means
author: Josh Holmberg
excerpt: Rats are mostly night animals, so seeing one in daylight tells you something. Here's what UF/IFAS and Florida DOH say a daytime rat can mean, and what to do next.

children.text: The short answer:

sometimes, and it's worth noticing. Rats are mainly active at night, so UF/IFAS says rodents seen again and again in daylight are a sign of an established population. Florida DOH says Norway rats may come out by day when numbers are high, when they're disturbed, or when food is threatened. Call (844) 264-6254.
When rats are normally active
Florida DOH says roof rats, the climbers that favor attics, are most active in the hour after sunset and the hour before dawn, and that Norway rats are mainly nocturnal and start moving about dusk (
Florida DOH
). UF/IFAS Extension notes that because rats are busiest at night, droppings and urine stains are usually the first signs people find, not the rats themselves (
UF/IFAS
Why you might see one by day
Crowding.
Florida DOH says some Norway rats come out in daylight when the population is high (
Florida DOH
). UF/IFAS puts it plainly: rodents seen repeatedly during the day point to an established population.
Disturbance.
DOH lists disturbance such as a change in the weather or construction nearby as another reason rats show up by day.
Food under threat.
DOH also names a threatened food source. That could be a cleaned-out shed, a new trash routine or a neighbor's cleanup.
What to check next
Droppings,
especially fresh ones after you've cleaned. The CDC says droppings that show up again after cleaning mean rats are still active (
CDC
Gnaw marks and grease stains
along pipes, wires and the holes rats use, which Florida DOH lists among the signs of an infestation.
Noise at night
in the attic or walls, the hours rats are normally out.
Food sources:
pet food, bird seed, fallen fruit and garbage within reach.
Our guides to
signs your house has rats
rats in the attic
and
what animal is in your attic
help confirm it.
What to do about it

One daytime sighting doesn't prove an infestation, but repeated ones usually mean there are more rats than you're seeing. UF/IFAS Extension describes three steps: rodent-proofing that blocks all possible entry points, sanitation, then reducing the population with traps and baits (
UF/IFAS
). Our guides on
how to catch a rat in the house
and

faq.question: Is it bad if I see a rat during the day?

children.text: It can be a warning sign. UF/IFAS Extension says rodents seen repeatedly during the day indicate an established population, because rats are mainly active at night.

faq.question: Why would a rat come out in daylight?

children.text: Florida DOH says Norway rats may be active by day when the population is high, when they're disturbed by things like weather changes or construction, or when their food source is threatened.

faq.question: What time are roof rats most active?

children.text: Florida DOH says roof rats are most active one hour after sunset and one hour before dawn.

faq.question: Do rats stay away from people?

children.text: They're mostly active when people are asleep, which is why droppings and gnaw marks are usually found before the rats. A rat seen often in daylight is a reason to look for an infestation.

title: Do Bats in Florida Carry Rabies? What the State's Numbers Show
author: Josh Holmberg
excerpt: Only a small share of bats have rabies, but some do, and Florida confirms dozens of rabid bats a year. Here's what Florida DOH's tables show, what FWC and the CDC say, and what to do after any contact.

children.text: The short answer:

some do. Florida DOH names raccoons and bats as the main wildlife sources of rabies in the state, and its tables list dozens of rabid bats a year. FWC says only a very small share of bats have it. Never handle a bat, and if one may have touched anyone, call your county health department. Call (844) 264-6254 for bats in the house.
What the state's tables show

children.text: No. FWC says only a very small share of bats have rabies, perhaps one among every few hundred. But because any bat could, the CDC says to avoid touching them.
